flows.name: Application boot
flows.summary: Wails embeds frontend assets, creates the Go app binding, loads persisted preferences through the bridge, and mounts the editor shell with a blank in-memory document.

steps.summary: The user launches the Wails application.
Wails binds the Go App object and startup hook.
The frontend asks for persisted settings and recent documents before applying runtime settings.
The Go API loads the JSON preference envelope from the user's config directory.
The embedded frontend assets mount the shell and blank document state.
The formatted editor mounts with an empty markdown document.

guarantees: Application opens to a blank document instead of sample content
Embedded app content does not duplicate the native window title bar
Persisted backed preferences apply before first user interaction
Recent documents render on the start screen when native storage has entries
failureBehavior: Wails logs startup/build errors in dev mode

flows.name: Open and save document
flows.summary: The frontend calls the Wails bridge, the Go API uses native dialogs or a recent path, Document IO reads or atomically writes markdown files, and the preference store records recents.
flows.trigger: User opens or saves a markdown document

steps.summary: The shell requests open, save, save-as, or unsaved-change resolution.
The bridge calls a bound Go method through Wails.
The Go API reads selected files or atomically writes saved content.
Successful open and save operations move the path to the top of the recent document list.
The shell updates document path, content, dirty state, file rail, and title state.

guarantees: Save writes atomically through the document package
Dirty buffers are guarded before open/close replacement
Recent documents are persisted after successful open and save flows
Recent documents can be reopened through a specific bridge method without showing the native picker
failureBehavior: Open/save failures show native error dialogs and do not discard dirty content

flows.name: Edit markdown document
flows.summary: The frontend shell maintains in-memory documents, routes ribbon/template interactions, renders backed assistant previews, and pushes dirty/content updates to the Wails API.
flows.trigger: User types or invokes a backed editor command

steps.summary: The user edits directly or applies a backed ribbon/template command.
The shell serializes or rebuilds the active formatted editor as needed.
Code block insertion opens a language chooser, while Mermaid Diagram insertion opens a type-specific assistant with live diagram preview.
Mermaid fenced blocks render as SVG diagrams in formatted and split preview surfaces.
The shell renders Split preview inline markdown semantics and shared code-block chrome without mutating source markdown.
The user hides or restores the left file rail and right document panel independently without changing the markdown buffer.
The shell pushes dirty state immediately and content after debounce.

guarantees: Visible enabled controls are backed by behavior
Formatting controls transform selected/current block content before insertion fallback
Code block insertion can declare a language from formatted mode
Mermaid fenced blocks render as diagrams instead of generic code blocks
Split preview renders common inline markdown syntax as document semantics
Rendered code blocks include language and Copy chrome
Left and right side panels can be hidden or restored independently without mutating markdown
Contextual document controls manage table, code-block language, and Mermaid Diagram assistance from the document surface
Contextual table and Mermaid Diagram controls target the selected rendered block when multiple matching blocks exist
Right-click and hover tools on existing code blocks open a language dialog for the acted-on fenced block
Print and PDF export render formatted markdown and invoke the OS print dialog without mutating markdown
failureBehavior: Unavailable future controls are removed from the current screen rather than faked

flows.name: Switch editor mode
flows.summary: The shell switches one active markdown buffer between formatted, raw, and split editor surfaces while preserving content.
flows.trigger: User chooses Formatted, Raw, or Split mode

steps.summary: The shell serializes the current editor before switching modes.
Raw mode mounts the highlighted source editor with raw options for soft wrap, line-number visibility, and markdown marker hiding.
The raw editor renders a synchronized tokenized markdown highlighting layer without changing the textarea source.
Formatted mode rebuilds Crepe from the current markdown buffer.

guarantees: Markdown round-trips across mode switches
Raw mode exposes only backed source-view controls
Raw and Split source modes can hide markdown marker glyphs without mutating source text
failureBehavior: Marker hiding keeps hidden marker width so textarea caret positions continue to align with raw source

flows.name: Configure runtime settings
flows.summary: The frontend shell opens a settings modal, loads installed font families through the native bridge, stages user preference changes in a draft, applies backed runtime preferences on Save, and persists them through the native preference store.
flows.trigger: User opens Settings from the primary ribbon tab row

steps.summary: The shell copies current runtime settings and raw options into a modal draft.
The shell asks the native app for installed font family names before rendering font controls.
The bridge calls the Wails-bound font listing method.
The Go API reads system and user font directories and normalizes family names.
The Go API returns sorted font family names discovered from system and user font directories.

The user changes staged default mode, formatted marker visibility, editor width, format-on-save, theme, document font, document font size, code font, code ligatures, soft-wrap, or line-number preferences.
Save applies the draft to body classes, CSS variables, and raw editor options.
The shell sends the saved preference envelope to the native app.
The Go API writes settings, raw options, and existing recents to the JSON preference file.
Cancel closes the modal without mutating runtime settings.

guarantees: Settings controls are backed by runtime behavior
Code font options come from native installed-font discovery when Wails bindings are available
Document and code font preferences apply to rendered editor surfaces
Backed preferences survive app relaunch
Cancel does not apply draft preferences
Future-only settings categories are visible but disabled
failureBehavior: Corrupt or unreadable preferences return native errors rather than being silently discarded
knownGaps: No Markdown flavour, Sync, Git, or Extensions settings yet
